shared.overview: No other BattleMech has captured imaginations in the Inner Sphere quite like the Atlas with its skull-like visage. It is among the largest and most imposing of the BattleMechs that have shaped the fate of humanity for the past half millennium. If its destructive potential is measured by its ability to level a city block, the Atlas reigns supreme. By all accounts, it is death incarnate, the king of all BattleMechs.:br::tab:There is another aspect to the symbolism attached to the Atlas. Unlike other high-end ’Mechs, most Atlas pilots chose to stay behind when General Aleksandr Kerensky called for the Exodus of the SLDF. Many of these juggernauts survived the Succession Wars. With Operation Revival, the Atlas became particularly tied to the fate of the Inner Sphere. It was the strongest bulwark Clan forces encountered in many battles. With this change in role of greatest destructor to greatest protector, the Atlas became a symbol of Inner Sphere resistance against the Clans and their OmniMechs.
shared.capabilities: There are constants in the Atlases over the centuries: a carefully crafted exterior befitting an instrument of destruction, high-end communications that make it an ideal command unit, and thick armor to support either role. Its armament invariably centers on a large ballistic weapon in the right torso. A visual quirk on most Atlases is the utilitarian coolant nozzle that mirrors the main weapon in the left torso. A hip-mounted LRM launcher is often mounted below it. The original’s quick-cycle system was never replicated in later variants. It currently houses smaller, tertiary weapons.:br::br::tab:Independence Weaponry took a long time to offer an upgrade to their Revival-era variant, which may have retained a dated heat dissipation system, but otherwise satisfied MechWarriors. The current model finally upgraded the heat sinks while also incorporating new armor and gyro options.:br::br::tab:Defiance Industries has continually produced and improved the Atlas. The Jihad and Word of Blake occupation resulted in the introduction of the Atlas II and a “mobility variant.” Three competing Atlas lines created a logistical inefficiency. The solution was to create a new variant that incorporates all the ClanTechequivalent systems Defiance offers.
shared.battleHistory: The little known Starseeker religious community in the deserts of Lahti had a problem with raiders in the summer of 3059. The tenets of their faith forbade them from engaging in violence—even in self-defense—and from possessing money with which to hire defenders. The peaceful people were resigned to turning over their entire moonfruit crop. Thus, they were surprised when an unknown Atlas appeared from the nearby rocky highlands and lumbered into the bandits. The ’Mech bore no insignia and broadcast no identification, but the pilot fought with great skill and determination. The raiders employed ramshackle and jury-rigged equipment, but their numbers proved a significant challenge to the Atlas. The peaceful Starseekers watched raptly as the single ’Mech worked its way through the bandit ranks before finally facing off with the only two ’Mechs in the enemy force: a Locust and a Shadow Hawk. The Atlas destroyed the Locust’s engine with an autocannon shot, but the Hawk proved more dangerous. The ’Mechs scored hits on each other and despite the Atlas’ superior weaponry and mass, the battle was touch and go. The Shadow Hawk pilot made the fatal mistake of getting too close. The Atlas managed to land a punch squarely on the cockpit, crushing the bandit MechWarrior. With the fight ended, the Atlas shut down and stood motionless outside the community’s gates.:br::br::tab:By February 3137, all that remained of Bannson’s Raiders was a couple of lances led by the unknown pilot of an old Atlas. Despite the command’s poor equipment and lack of formal military training, they managed to evade Republic authorities on seven worlds before being cornered on Altair by Stone’s Lament. The battle, of course, was incredibly lopsided, but surprisingly the Raiders’ leader proved a worthy opponent. He kicked off the fight by crippling a Lament Wight with a Gauss slug to the shoulder. The Atlas was in the heart of the conflict and rapidly became a focus of the Lament’s efforts. Even so, the pilot personally accounted for six Lament ’Mechs. A Lament Malice delivered the killing blow, finally causing the Atlas to collapse. The pilot did not survive and was never identified. He was however celebrated by the Lament MechWarriors as a commendable foe.
shared.variants: In the 3060s, Defiance Industries quickly introduced the AS7-S3 alongside their earlier heavy Gauss rifle variant, which reverted to more conventional but powerful weaponry. Deemed exactly equal in capability, both were produced concurrently in the years since. The later AS7-4 retained the majority of the -S3’s armament, but married it to stealth armor. These were all produced alongside the Atlas II and faster models, until a recent program combined their best attributes into the -8S.:br::br::tab:The Lyrans were as eager to utilize the Atlas’s command capabilities as their Combine counterparts. The Commonwealth focused on the use of command consoles. Initial attempts upgraded the AS7-K, introduced en masse to the Federated Commonwealth while on relatively good terms with the Combine in the 3050s. The resulting -S3-DC became the main command Atlas a decade later.:br::br::tab:Independence offers an export version of their -8K, which uses a standard engine at the expense of some secondary weaponry.:br::br::tab:The Clans had few Atlases. Nevertheless, a rudimentary refit protocol was created for the Atlas C, which upgraded the weapons, and was later commonly implemented on captured Inner Sphere Atlases during Operation Revival. A more thorough upgrade that replaced the LRMs with an additional ER PPC was later implemented on most Atlases and Atlas IIs in Clan space. The few remaining chassis replaced their LRMs with Arrow IV artillery pieces. All our ArcShips can perform both upgrades on most existing Atlas chassis.
shared.notableUnits: Precentor Martial Anastasius Focht: The man born Frederick Steiner rose from the fires of his own treachery to forge a reputation both as the man who beat the Clans and who failed to stop the rise of the Word of Blake. The road to his new life as Focht began on Dromini VI in late 3029 with the Tenth Lyran Guards’ attempt to disrupt Theodore Kurita’s preparations for an assault into the Commonwealth. Forgoing his Zeus for an Atlas, Steiner led his troops in a suicidal attack on the DCMS supply base. He fought with characteristic skill, tinged with a hint of feral abandon. The disgraced commander was determined to inflict as much damage as possible before his inevitable death. Yet when it became clear that the Guards had reached the limit of their assault, Steiner nobly offered his surrender to guarantee the safe withdrawal of his people. Though Frederick Steiner died that day, Anastasius Focht took the lessons learned and became one of the Inner Sphere’s greatest leaders since the Great Father.:br:MechWarrior Liam Miguel Loyola: Once the Starseekers on Lahti worked up the courage to approach the dormant Atlas that had saved their community, they found an unconscious man in the cockpit. He was unknown to them and no identifying uniform or documentation were found. The only clue to his identity was the name Liam Miguel Loyola on his cooling vest and a silver pendant necklace with the letters “LLL” around his neck. After waking up and being treated for his injuries, the man remembered nothing. Loyola politely declined to join the Starseeker faith, though he remained near the community, knowing that the peaceful people would always need his protection.:br:Leftenant Richard West II: House West is a minor noble clan dating to the earliest settlement on New Avalon. Ardent supporters of the Davions, they have supplied the Federated Suns with countless soldiers and officers over the centuries. Richard had just posted to the Davion Heavy Guards when Katherine Steiner stripped the RCT of its transport assets, stranding the Guards on Galax until Prince Victor’s push to retake New Avalon staged from that world. West piloted an Atlas that had been in his family for two hundred years as he personally led the assault that liberated his hometown on the continent of Brunswick.:br:MechWarrior James Andreou: Andreou grew up idolizing MechWarriors as a modern knighthood. The then-Leftenant was horrified when his commanding officer in the Bremond DMM ordered him to execute several surrendered Blakist soldiers. He was arrested for refusing to follow orders but sprung that night by several comrades. The group stole their BattleMechs and fled to a rendezvous with a trader they paid to get them off-world. The group fell out over money while looking for work as mercenaries on Antallos. In the ensuing fight, Andreou’s Atlas suffered what he thought was minor damage. However, as he hired himself out as a lone gunslinger, the Atlas never quite worked right again and nearly every credit he earned went toward keeping it patched and running. Despite this, Andreou forged a reputation and career as an honorable, if not flashy, warrior.:br:Knight Duncan Kalma: Early in the Jihad, degenerate gambler-turned-Knight Duncan Kalma rescued his father moments before a Blakist team scooped up the former intelligence director. Kalma made his way off world and led a reformed Duncan’s Demons, cobbled together from whatever MechWarriors he could get. The command fought a number of guerrilla actions against Blakists throughout the Free Worlds League over the next several years. An Atlas may not be ideal for such missions, but Duncan made it work, becoming an essential piece of Alys Rousset-Marik’s resistance group. Duncan survived the Jihad but vanished shortly after his father’s death, two weeks after the official proclamation of the Marik-Stewart Commonwealth. His ultimate fate is unknown.:br:Commander Sean Armstrong: Armstrong was formerly chair of Austen-Armstrong Industries’ board of directors. His fortunes slipped away over the course of a financially ruinous decade. The loss of the company’s Bainsville plant to Clan Wolf, followed by the takeover of Abadan by the Clan Protectorate, sent AARMS stocks into a deep downward spiral. The remaining AustenArmstrong directors lost confidence in Armstrong and launched a corporate coup to oust him from his hereditary position. Bereft of his once-formidable salary and now holding worthless investments, Armstrong decided to levy his influential family name as part of a new mercenary venture. His imposing and well-upgraded Atlas was welcomed by every mercenary outfit he approached. Watch agents last spotted him on Galatea making overtures to the rapidly building Bleeding Eagles command.:br:SaKhan Ya’el Labov: In the initial Amaterasu assault on Tahlwynn’s spaceport on Dieron, saKhan Ya’el Labov was injured when her Atlas’ cockpit suffered a glancing blow from a damaged crane. She managed to pilot her ’Mech during the retreat into the mountains, but she was out of action for several weeks as Exarch Damien Redburn led Republic forces and Labov’s own Sea Fox troops against the invaders. Even after she returned to the field, Labov functioned more as an observer. She was often perched above the action in her Atlas for a strategic overview of the battle. During the final push to retake Dieron’s capital, she again entered the fray and proved her skill when she stepped between an Amaterasu Atlas and Damien Redburn’s downed Black Knight. SaKhan Labov made quick work of her foe and saved the Exarch’s life.:br:Representative Rolf Christian Steiner: Rolf Steiner is a hero to the people of Loxley, as a man of royal blood who bends the Estates General to his will. To his peers, however, Steiner is nothing more than a running joke that has yet to run out of breath. Political opponents routinely discover that he is quick to take affront. The representative wastes no time issuing challenges to “fight things out as real Lyrans” at the helm of their ’Mechs. Curiously, Steiner has yet to appear at even one of his so-called duels. His Atlas is always one part away from functionality, forcing Rolf to postpone all his fights. This has done little to whittle his popular base, though. To his supporters, Steiner will doubtlessly prove himself once his Atlas is fully operational. His opponents, meanwhile, openly mock his 1–7 record—his only “win” was the result of the untimely death of his very elderly adversary.:br:Captain Jeremy West: West was born on Ozawa and raised on tales of the exploits of his ancestors. His father regaled him with stories of his Wolf’s Dragoons forebears while his mother, of Nova Cat descent, instilled in him a sense of pride for his heritage. He was swept up by Senator Kev Rosse’s impassioned speeches in the early 3130s. He joined the nascent Spirit Cats, taking on the West surname, and departed for Outreach alongside a small Dragoons contingent. He met warriors from the legendary mercenary command for the first time and found himself torn between his two heritages. It was undeniable by all, however, that the discovery of a sizable cache on Remus was fate’s clear answer for him—he himself stumbled across the battered hulk of the Atlas once piloted by his greatgrandmother, Ariana Foster. West became certain that his future lay with the Dragoons. He departed with them to craft his own legend with the storied command.

shared: The Avalanche is a medium Inner Sphere OmniMech introduced in 3133 by Luthien Armor Works on Luthien. Conceived as a joint development between the Draconis Combine and Clan Nova Cat in the aftermath of the Second Combine-Dominion War, the design was intended to rebuild the Clan's depleted touman while providing the DCMS with a cost-effective trooper OmniMech. Built entirely from off-the-shelf Inner Sphere components, the Avalanche fills a niche as an economical medium OmniMech prioritizing reliability and ease of maintenance over raw performance. Production has continued on Luthien through the Dark Age and into the ilClan era, with exports reaching the Capellan Confederation and mercenary markets following Clan Nova Cat's destruction.

The Avalanche prioritizes economy and maintainability over cutting-edge performance. Built on a Luthien Class M endo steel chassis, the design employs a standard Hermes 250 fusion engine providing a maximum speed of 86 kilometers per hour, adequate but unexceptional for a fifty-ton platform. Five Icarus Standard jump jets enhance tactical mobility with a jump capacity of 150 meters, while ten tons of Mitchel Argon Standard armor provides reasonable protection, though less than many contemporary medium designs. Ten double heat sinks manage thermal loads across most configurations, and CASE protection in the right torso guards against catastrophic ammunition detonation.

The chassis allocates sixteen tons of pod space, offering decent reconfiguration flexibility for a medium OmniMech. A significant design flaw manifests when Clan-manufactured weapons are installed: the Matabushi Stalker targeting system loses alignment after extended use, with Nova Cat warriors reporting misalignment reaching two full degrees during gunnery exercises, a deficiency that severely undermined confidence in the platform and ultimately led to its abandonment by Clan Nova Cat in favor of the purpose-built Wendigo.

The Avalanche emerged from the aftermath of the Second Combine-Dominion War, which ended in 3101 and left Clan Nova Cat's military forces severely depleted. The DCMS granted Luthien Armor Works carte blanche to collaborate with the Clan on a jointly developed OmniMech that would be economical to produce using readily available resources. What followed was one of the longest development cycles in modern BattleMech history, with the project plagued by three decades of false starts, reappropriated funding, and unresolved technical challenges before the first Avalanche rolled off LAW's production line in 3133.

The design was deployed shortly before the Draconis Combine's invasion of the Republic of the Sphere, seeing action with elite formations including the Sword of Light and Benjamin Regulars. A lance of Avalanches from the Sixth Benjamin Regulars participated in a hot-drop onto Shinonoi to secure the primary landing zone, engaging targets from long range with Clan technology before reconfiguring to support capital defense operations. The DCMS found the Avalanche to be a serviceable trooper OmniMech, but Clan Nova Cat's warrior caste was far less satisfied. Persistent targeting system malfunctions with Clan weaponry frustrated Nova Cat warriors to the point where the Clan developed only two mixed-technology configurations before abandoning the platform entirely, opting instead to create the Wendigo, a purely Clan-built OmniMech based on the Avalanche's chassis.

Following the destruction of Clan Nova Cat after its revolt against Coordinator Yori Kurita, the dead Clan's allotment of Avalanches was redistributed. Luthien Armor Works refurbished former Nova Cat machines and channeled them through the Clan's export division, where Clan Sea Fox, the Capellan Confederation, and the Free Worlds League expressed interest. The Confederation purchased a significant number of Avalanches prior to its invasion of the Federated Suns, deploying them extensively in the conquest of Capellan March worlds. Sea Fox merchants resold additional units to mercenary companies, where the solidly-built 'Mech found favor among smaller outfits that valued its reliability and ease of maintenance over raw combat performance.

shared: The Avatar is a seventy-ton Inner Sphere OmniMech born from the Draconis Combine's ambitious effort to reverse-engineer Clan technology following the Battle of Luthien in 3052. Luthien Armor Works began development using captured Mad Dog OmniMechs as the basis for the design, making the Avatar the first Inner Sphere OmniMech conceptualized. Prolonged integration difficulties between Clan and Inner Sphere technologies, however, meant it was among the last of the Combine's first generation OmniMechs to enter production in 3056. Filling the role of a versatile heavy fire support platform, the Avatar leverages a generous thirty-four tons of pod space to accommodate a wide variety of weapon configurations. Licensed production through StarCorps Industries, Victory Industries, and General Motors has spread the design across multiple Successor States, establishing it as one of the most widely manufactured Inner Sphere OmniMechs in service.

The Avatar's chassis mounts a Hermes 280 XL engine, providing a top speed of sixty-four kilometers per hour. While especially slower than its Clan-designed ancestor, this trade-off in mobility purchases considerably more internal volume and pod capacity than the original Mad Dog offered. With thirty-four tons of available pod space, the Avatar can mount firepower rivaling many assault-weight designs while retaining the tactical flexibility inherent to OmniMech technology. Twelve tons of StarSlab/4 armor provide respectable protection for its weight class, supplemented by CASE systems in both side torsos to mitigate the catastrophic risk of ammunition detonation.

A distinctive feature of the design is its two permanently mounted Victory 23R medium lasers in the center torso. These hardwired weapons trace their origin to early testing phases when OmniPod connector faults risked leaving the entire weapons array disabled. Though the underlying issue was resolved before deployment, the fixed lasers remain as a design vestige ensuring the Avatar is never completely unarmed. In its Prime configuration, the Avatar combines an LB 10-X autocannon with dual LRM-10 launchers equipped with Artemis IV fire control, supplemented by medium pulse lasers and machine guns for a balanced loadout emphasizing ranged engagement with credible close-in capability.

The Avatar's genesis lies in the aftermath of the Battle of Luthien in 3052, when the Draconis Combine Mustered Soldiery found itself in possession of significant Clan salvage but unable to maintain the captured equipment. Within months, the majority of trophy Clan machines in DCMS service were rendered combat ineffective due to maintenance failures. Luthien Armor Works was tasked with finding a practical solution, and their engineers responded by combining captured Vulture components with Inner Sphere technology. The process of melding the two tech bases proved far more difficult than anticipated, and while the Raptor, Owens, and Black Hawk-KU all reached service first, the Avatar's troubled development ultimately produced one of the Combine's most capable and enduring OmniMech designs.

Initial production during the late 3050s went primarily to DCMS units stationed along the Clan border, with limited quantities sold to ComStar and the Federated Commonwealth for deployment in the Lyran half's Clan frontier. The secession of the Lyran Alliance in 3057 prompted the Combine to redirect the reserved FedCom allotment to ComStar instead, an arrangement that persisted through the conclusion of the First Combine-Dominion War. The Davion half of the rump Federated Commonwealth instead received output from locally licensed production, as StarCorps Industries plants on Crofton, Son Hoa, St. Ives, and Loburg brought the Avatar into broader Successor State service during the 3060s. General Motors began production at New Valencia, and Victory Industries on Marduk received a subcontract from Luthien Armor Works, further broadening the manufacturing base within Combine borders.

This distributed production network proved critical when the Word of Blake's assault on Luthien during the opening years of the Jihad resulted in the nuclear destruction of Luthien Armor Works' massive OmniMech production complex. The Guthry Island facility where the Avatar and other OmniMechs were built was reportedly obliterated in the midst of a simultaneous Black Dragon coup, eliminating the design's primary production line along with capacity for several other Combine OmniMechs. The loss was compounded by the destruction of General Motors' facilities on Kathil. However, the surviving StarCorps and Victory Industries lines ensured the Avatar's continued production, albeit at reduced volume.

The Avatar remains in active service across multiple Successor States well into the post-Jihad era. Its widespread distribution across the Draconis Combine, Federated Suns, Lyran Commonwealth, and Capellan Confederation ensures that the design continues to see regular deployment along numerous frontiers, evidence of both the robustness of its engineering and the foresight of its licensing arrangements.

shared:
The BTL-C-2O Battle Cobra represents ComStar's troubled but ultimately successful effort to reverse-engineer Clan OmniMech technology. Following the Battle of Tukayyid in 3052, ComStar recovered numerous Battle Cobra chassis from the fighting in the Devil's Bath, selecting the design as the foundation for their OmniMech development program. Progress was severely hampered by the Word of Blake schism, which saw many of ComStar's top scientists and engineers defect, leaving inexperienced personnel to manage one of the organization's most ambitious technological projects. The loss of Terra to the Word of Blake in 3058 further devastated ComStar's industrial base, but also created the urgency that drove the remaining technical teams to complete the simplest viable OmniMech at any cost. The BTL-C-2O reached full production in 3063, manufactured at ComStar's Tukayyid facility and later at Arc-Royal MechWorks.

Especially, the Word of Blake's parallel Battle Cobra research, eventually entrusted to Devon Cortland, would gradually evolve into the first of the notorious Celestial OmniMechs, the Preta.

The adaptation of the Battle Cobra to Inner Sphere technology forced several significant compromises. The bulkier frame resulted in an astonishingly cramped chassis, and the late decision to integrate ComStar's cutting-edge C3i networking system necessitated downsizing to a Nissan 200 fusion engine. This reduced the design's top speed to just eighty-six kilometers per hour, substantially slower than its Clan progenitor. The regenerative cooling system demanded by the C3i integration required bulky heat sinks that further crowded the already tight torso compartments, creating maintenance nightmares for ComStar technicians.

These compromises did yield unexpected benefits. The tightly packed internal layout meant that shots which would normally penetrate to the fusion engine were instead absorbed by intervening components, giving the BTL-C-2O surprising durability for its weight class. The smaller engine also freed sufficient mass to provide seventeen and a half tons of pod space, actually exceeding the Clan original's fourteen tons of capacity. Most configurations carried the C3i computer as standard equipment, transforming the Battle Cobra from an independent combatant into a networked support platform that excelled when operating as part of a coordinated lance or Level II formation.

The result was an OmniMech that struggled in direct confrontation with contemporary designs but proved highly effective in its intended conventional support role.

ComStar's Battle Cobra program was born from the unprecedented access to Clan technology gained at Tukayyid, yet its development became emblematic of the organization's post-Schism institutional failures. While the Draconis Combine successfully leveraged similar salvage from Wolcott and Luthien into a functioning OmniMech program, ComStar's efforts floundered as the Word of Blake schism stripped away their most talented engineers and scientists. The capture of Terra in 3058 compounded the crisis, destroying ComStar's primary industrial base and forcing leadership to order the completion of whatever OmniMech project could be finished fastest. The Battle Cobra, with its straightforward arm-mounted pod system, won this grim competition by default.

Production began at ComStar's Tukayyid Omega-Epsilon Facility X in 3063, but the factory's existence made it an immediate target when the Word of Blake Jihad erupted. Orbital bombardment destroyed the Tukayyid facility in 3068, leaving ComStar with little more than the design's schematics. A hastily negotiated partnership with Arc-Royal MechWorks provided a new production line, though the struggling manufacturer required years to deliver the troublesome OmniMech reliably.

The ComStar Battle Cobra's finest hour came during the Fourth Army's assault on Chertan, where two Level IIs of the design led operations against entrenched Word of Blake Protectorate Militia. Working in concert with battle armor scouts in a formation inspired by the Blakist Choir doctrine, the Battle Cobras demonstrated the design's true strength, rapid reconfiguration between engagements allowed commanders to tailor each machine's loadout to the tactical situation, switching between TAG-equipped spotter configurations and direct-fire assault packages as conditions demanded.

Despite proving essential in the liberation of Chertan and other Protectorate worlds, front-line service steadily eroded the Battle Cobra's numbers. The dissolution of the Com Guards following the Jihad's conclusion cost Arc-Royal MechWorks its primary customer, and the manufacturer eventually shuttered the production line around 3090 to focus on more profitable designs, including the restored Verfolger line. With the original Clan Battle Cobra now rolling off Arc-Royal's restored production lines under Jade Falcon ownership, the days of the Inner Sphere variant appear numbered, though the few mercenary commands still operating them praise the design's rugged versatility.

The BTL-C-2O Battle Cobra represents ComStar's troubled but ultimately successful effort to reverse-engineer Clan OmniMech technology. Following the Battle of Tukayyid in 3052, ComStar recovered numerous Battle Cobra chassis from the fighting in the Devil's Bath, selecting the design as the foundation for their OmniMech development program. Progress was severely hampered by the Word of Blake schism, which saw many of ComStar's top scientists and engineers defect, leaving inexperienced personnel to manage one of the organization's most ambitious technological projects. The loss of Terra to the Word of Blake in 3058 further devastated ComStar's industrial base, but also created the urgency that drove the remaining technical teams to complete the simplest viable OmniMech at any cost. The BTL-C-2O reached full production in 3063, manufactured at ComStar's Tukayyid facility and later at Arc-Royal MechWorks.

Particularly, the Word of Blake's parallel Battle Cobra research, eventually entrusted to Devon Cortland, would gradually evolve into the first of the notorious Celestial OmniMechs, the Preta.

text.overview: It is hard to imagine too many Atlases could ever be a problem for anyone on their side of the battlefield, but that was precisely the situation faced by Defiance Industries. Production lines operated for no less than three branches, each marketed by a different division of the company and sometimes directly competing with each other. The program that led to production of the AS8-S solved this problem but created a new one: a massive stockpile of superfluous Atlas components. Defiance’s solution was to use off-the-shelf components, in a limited-run variant that combined the Atlas II with the engine of the AS7-K2. This AS7-DK-H model proved so successful that it remains in production.
text.notableUnits: Commander Murdock Billingsham: Billingsham commands of a small band of mercenaries operating since Gray Monday. He never lacks for work as he moves the command from one brushfire conflict to another. He participated in virtually every major conflict since 3132, sometimes on both sides, due to his preference for short-term contracts that preserve his freedom of action. In an age of small militaries, employers desperate to bolster their forces rarely object to his terms, at least until he negotiates a contract with the enemy over open comms the moment his current one expires, as he did on Victoria during the Capellan invasion. Billingsham is famously unafraid in battle, confident the speed and armor of his massive Atlas II will protect him.

text.deployment: Designed as a dedicated long-range combatant, the B configuration mounts a light PPC and ER medium laser in each arm, providing sustained energy fire without ammunition dependency. Thunderbolt 5 missile launchers in each side torso supplement the energy package with guided missile fire, fed by two tons of ammunition in the right torso. This configuration maximizes the Avalanche's effective engagement distance while maintaining energy weapons as a fallback when missiles are depleted, making it well-suited for extended operations where resupply is uncertain.

Built around a ballistic weapons platform, the C configuration mounts a light AC/5 in each arm alongside ER medium lasers, providing a versatile mix of autocannon and energy fire at medium ranges. Small X-Pulse lasers in the side torsos serve as close-range deterrents against lighter units that attempt to exploit the Avalanche's modest speed. This configuration excels in sustained engagements where the light autocannons' efficient ammunition consumption allows prolonged operations without resupply, making it a popular choice for garrison and patrol duties.

One of only two mixed-technology configurations developed in cooperation with Clan Nova Cat, the N configuration centers on a single torso-mounted Clan ER PPC linked to a targeting computer, delivering precise long-range energy fire with enhanced accuracy. A right arm-mounted light AC/5 with generous ammunition stores provides secondary ballistic support. Despite the targeting computer's intended role in compensating for the Matabushi Stalker system's known alignment issues with Clan weapons, Nova Cat warriors reported that the fundamental incompatibility persisted, contributing to the Clan's eventual abandonment of the platform in favor of the purpose-built Wendigo.

The second and more ambitious of the Nova Cat mixed-technology configurations, the R mounts exclusively Clan-manufactured weapons including a Clan LRM-10 launcher for long-range fire support and paired ATM-3 launchers offering tactical flexibility through their multi-munition capability. Clan ER medium lasers in each arm round out the loadout with efficient energy fire. Though the most capable Avalanche configuration on paper, the R suffered most acutely from the targeting system alignment problems, as every weapon in the configuration relied on the Clan-incompatible interface that plagued the design throughout its Nova Cat service.

The Alternate Configuration A transforms the Avatar into a dedicated close-combat brawler. An ER large laser provides its sole long-range capability, while an Autocannon/20 and paired SRM-6 launchers deliver devastating short-range firepower. Four jump jets grant the normally ground-bound chassis unexpected mobility, allowing MechWarriors to exploit terrain and close rapidly with targets. This combination of jump capability and overwhelming close-range punch makes the A configuration particularly effective as an anti-Elemental platform and urban warfare combatant.

The Alternate Configuration BLO is a custom loadout developed for the Blessed Order's revived First Division as part of the Unending Faith III formation. Based on the E configuration, the BLO retains the improved C3 computer and Guardian ECM suite while replacing the primary armament with an ER PPC in the left arm and an LB 10-X autocannon in the right. Four jump jets provide tactical mobility not found in the standard E configuration, allowing the BLO variant to exploit terrain while maintaining electronic warfare capability. The combination of network coordination, electronic protection, and enhanced mobility makes this a purpose-built formation command platform.

The Alternate Configuration C is built around a C3 master computer, enabling the Avatar to serve as the central coordination node for a networked lance. Offensive armament consists of a PPC and Ultra Autocannon/5 for ranged engagement, supported by dual LRM-10 launchers. This combination of command capability and solid ranged firepower positions the C configuration as a natural command platform for combined-arms formations operating under the Draconis Combine's C3 doctrine.

The Alternate Configuration D incorporates technology sourced from both the Free Worlds League and the Draconis Combine to fill a dedicated sniper role. A light Gauss rifle provides extreme-range precision fire at seven hundred and fifty meters, while paired MRM-20 launchers and two ER medium lasers handle closer engagements. A C3 slave unit allows the D configuration to share targeting data within a networked lance, enhancing the accuracy of its already formidable long-range armament. Two additional double heat sinks manage the thermal load of sustained fire.

The Alternate Configuration E was developed for use by ComStar and the Word of Blake, reflecting their distinctive technological preferences. An ER PPC serves as the primary weapon, supported by an Ultra Autocannon/10 and an ER medium laser. The configuration's defining feature is its improved C3 computer paired with a Guardian ECM suite, providing both network coordination capability and electronic warfare protection. Six additional double heat sinks allow aggressive use of the energy-heavy armament, making the E configuration a capable electronic warfare platform that can hold its own in direct combat.

The Alternate Configuration F pairs an ER PPC with an LB 20-X autocannon for a straightforward but potent combination of long-range precision and devastating close-range firepower. The LB 20-X's ability to fire cluster ammunition makes this configuration particularly dangerous to lighter targets at short range. Jump jets provide tactical mobility unusual for the Avatar chassis, and five extra double heat sinks ensure the energy weapons can be fired continuously without overheating concerns. The F configuration's simplicity and raw hitting power make it a favored choice for MechWarriors who prefer direct engagement.

The Alternate Configuration G is a dedicated heavy fire support platform mounting a Gauss rifle in each arm with two tons of ammunition per weapon. This paired Gauss arrangement delivers exceptional long-range kinetic damage without generating significant waste heat, allowing sustained fire at extreme distances. The G configuration sacrifices weapon variety and close-range capability entirely in favor of concentrated long-range striking power, making it best employed in fire support lances where lighter units can screen against enemies that close to short range.

Developed during the Jihad, the Alternate Configuration H mounts a heavy PPC in each arm, providing formidable direct-fire capability at medium to long range. Two MML-3 launchers equipped with Artemis IV fire control systems offer supplementary fire with the flexibility to load either long-range or short-range missile ammunition as tactical conditions dictate. Sixteen double heat sinks manage the considerable thermal output of the twin heavy PPCs, though sustained Alpha strikes still generate significant excess heat.

The Alternate Configuration I employs twin Thunderbolt 15 missile launchers mounted in the torso, delivering heavy guided missile strikes at extended range. Each launcher carries two tons of ammunition, providing adequate endurance for prolonged engagements. ER medium lasers in each arm supplement the missile armament at closer ranges, while sixteen double heat sinks keep thermal levels manageable. The Thunderbolt missiles' single-target impact profile makes this configuration particularly effective against hardened targets and fortifications.

The Alternate Configuration J stands as a significant escalation in firepower, mounting a Hyper-Assault Gauss 30 in each arm with eight tons of ammunition stored in CASE-protected bays. The paired HAG/30 weapons deliver withering streams of hypervelocity projectiles capable of shredding armor at extended range, giving the J configuration one of the highest sustained damage outputs available to any Avatar loadout. Introduced in the post-Jihad era, this configuration reflects advances in weapons miniaturization that allow such heavy armament to fit within the Avatar's pod space constraints.

The Alternate Configuration R is a field upgrade developed during Operation Bulldog, utilizing captured Clan Smoke Jaguar weapons to bolster SLDF forces in the later waves of the offensive. Mounting a mix of Combine and Clan technology, this configuration carries an MRM-40 for devastating medium-range salvos alongside a Clan-specification Gauss rifle for long-range precision. A Clan ER large laser and Streak SRM-4 round out the armament. The R configuration's mixed-technology loadout represents one of the earliest practical applications of integrating captured Clan weaponry into Inner Sphere OmniMech platforms under combat conditions.

text.overview: With Johnston’s facilities undamaged during the Capellans’ ejection from New Syrtis, the company expanded production as much as possible to prop up the faltering Davion military. Their new Axman was just a prototype in 3146, and only a lack of components stopped the Capellans from putting it into full production. Sharing a number of components with the Caesar -5D and Hatchetman -7D, the new Axman -5N is a terror at any range. The Tiburon Khanate-supplied HAG 20 and ER PPC allow it to deal damage as it closes, while triple ER medium lasers deal significant short-range damage. These weapons provide a number of ways to activate the ’Mech’s triple-strength myomers, allowing the -5N to close quicker and deal unholy amounts of damage in close combat.
text.notableUnits: Si-ben-bing Sewarion Smirnow: A recent graduate from the Victoria Academy of Arms and Technology on Gunthar, Smirnow was thrust into the limelight during the Davion re-conquest of New Syrtis. After his Vindicator was damaged early in the battle, he acquired one of the Axman -5N prototypes to carry on the fight, and scythed his way through nearly two lances of the Illician Lancers’ Fifty-Ninth Striker Regiment as they tried to storm the Saso spaceport.:br::br::tab:Eventually forced to retreat, Smirnow and a few stragglers carried on guerrilla attacks against the Davions for another two months before retreating off-world in late February 3148. He would later put the ’Mech to good use against the Republic during the Operation Bàoyìng attacks the following year on Terra Firma, helping to finish off the second battalion of the Thirteenth Principes.

text.overview: The new Banshee is the latest stage of evolution that began with the BNC-3S. The -12S builds upon the endo-steel chassis of prior models, upgrading it with a home-built Clan-grade engine and lasers. The weight savings enabled Defiance’s engineers to follow the weaponry layout of the -3S. Armor levels match the toughest Banshees, creating a very strong and fast assault ’Mech, albeit one with a challenging heat curve. Alpha-striking will shut the ’Mech down, so MechWarriors are advised to use either the main or secondary weapons, but not both at once.
text.notableUnits: Hauptmann Christopher Cain: Cain was a green leutnant fresh from the academy when he was assigned to the newly reformed Eighth Lyran Guards. The Eighth specialized in Republic of the Sphere tactics and served as an OpFor for training other Lyran units. Thus, they were woefully unprepared for the Jade Falcon desant on Porrima in 3134. Barely a quarter of the regiment escaped the slaughter. His father and son were killed when Galaxy Commander Aleksandr Hazen razed a district of Allison City after an unsuccessful assassination attempt, though the Falcons eventually decided not to hold the world.:br::br::tab:Cain is now a battle-hardened veteran. He was promoted while the unit slowly rebuilt. The Eighth refused to leave Porrima during the tenure of Archon Brewer. They later absorbed the remnants of the Sixth Guards following the battle of Tharkad. The Eighth is now based on Veckholm where Cain commands a company—Cain’s Cavaliers. His deep-seated hatred for the Falcons is surpassed only by his sense of duty to his MechWarriors, all of whom are survivors of battles against the Clans.

text.deployment: The baseline configuration mirrors its Clan counterpart's approach by mounting an Inner Sphere-grade large pulse laser in each arm, supplemented by an extra double heat sink and the standard C3i networking computer. While the pulse lasers lack the range and efficiency of their Clan equivalents, the C3i system allows this variant to share targeting data across its formation, partially compensating for the individual weapon downgrade through superior coordination. This configuration served as the workhorse of ComStar Battle Cobra formations throughout the design's operational history.

An electronic warfare specialist, Alternate Configuration A carries a comprehensive sensor and countermeasures suite including a Guardian ECM suite, Beagle active probe, and TAG designator alongside its C3i computer. Offensive armament consists of three medium pulse lasers and a small pulse laser in the left arm with three standard medium lasers in the right, providing adequate self-defense capability. This configuration transforms the Battle Cobra into a dedicated reconnaissance and electronic support platform, capable of disrupting enemy sensor networks while designating targets for allied indirect fire assets.

A medium-range missile boat, Alternate Configuration B mounts a pair of MRM-10 launchers in each arm fed by three tons of ammunition, enhanced by the standard C3i networking computer. The MRM launchers deliver respectable salvos at medium ranges without the minimum range limitations of standard LRM systems, making this configuration effective in the urban and close-terrain environments where ComStar frequently deployed the design during the Jihad.

A specialized spotter configuration, Alternate Configuration C dedicates both arms to improved Narc missile beacon launchers, carrying five tons of varied ammunition types alongside the standard C3i networking computer. While mounting no other weapons of any kind, the extensive ammunition supply allows operators to employ every conceivable iNarc warhead variant, from homing beacons to explosive pods. This configuration reaches its full potential when operating alongside missile-heavy formations that can exploit the iNarc designations.

Developed during the early years of the Jihad, Alternate Configuration D mounts a pair of light PPCs in each arm, all linked to both a targeting computer and C3i system. The targeting computer enhances the already-accurate light particle cannons to exceptional precision, while the four-PPC broadside provides consistent energy-based firepower without ammunition dependency. This configuration proved popular with Com Guard commanders who valued sustainable firepower during extended campaigns where resupply was uncertain.

Taking advantage of Multi-Missile Launcher technology, Alternate Configuration E mounts an MML-9 in each arm, carrying two tons of LRM ammunition and one ton of SRM missiles alongside the standard C3i computer. The MML system's ability to fire either long-range or short-range missiles from the same launcher gives this configuration unusual tactical flexibility, allowing pilots to adapt their engagement range without the need for full pod reconfiguration.

A dedicated anti-infantry and area-denial configuration, Alternate Configuration F mounts a plasma rifle in each arm with three tons of ammunition, rounded out by the standard C3i networking system. The plasma rifles deliver devastating thermal damage that is particularly effective against conventional infantry and light vehicles, while the superheated plasma bolts can significantly degrade the combat effectiveness of even heavily armored opponents through heat transfer.

A post-Jihad configuration developed after the dissolution of the Com Guards, Alternate Configuration G carries a Snub-Nose PPC in the right arm and a plasma rifle in the left, each supported by a machine gun. Three tons of plasma rifle ammunition and a ton of machine gun rounds are protected by CASE II in the right torso, with an additional double heat sink managing the thermal load. This mixed-weapon approach provides effective firepower across a broad range of engagement distances, reflecting the mercenary operators who adopted the design after ComStar's disbandment.

Another post-Jihad design, Alternate Configuration H centers its firepower around a Thunderbolt 15 launcher in the right arm supported by three ER medium lasers. Three tons of Thunderbolt missile ammunition split between the right arm and torso provide reasonable endurance, while standard CASE protects against catastrophic ammunition detonation. The Thunderbolt's ability to deliver concentrated single-point damage makes this configuration effective at breaching weakened armor sections from medium range.

A Dark Age-era configuration representing the final evolution of the Inner Sphere Battle Cobra line, Alternate Configuration J carries a large re-engineered laser in the right arm and a medium re-engineered laser paired with an ER medium laser in the left. All weapons are linked to a targeting computer for enhanced accuracy, while a supercharger allows the normally sluggish Battle Cobra to achieve brief bursts of higher speed when closing with targets. A left-arm mounted M-Pod provides a last-ditch close-range deterrent.

text.overview: The BattleMaster is one of the most iconic assault 'Mechs in the history of the Inner Sphere, first rolling off the production lines of Hollis Industries on Corey in 2633. Originally commissioned by the Star League as a powerful frontline command platform for non-Royal unit commanders, the eighty-five-ton design combined devastating close-range firepower with the sophisticated cockpit electronics necessary to coordinate company- and battalion-level operations. The sheer cost and complexity of the BattleMaster limited production to a handful of worlds, yet those fortunate enough to pilot one quickly discovered a 'Mech whose reputation for reliability, survivability, and raw combat presence was well earned. Affectionately dubbed the "Beemer" by generations of MechWarriors, the BattleMaster has endured centuries of warfare, serving in the arsenals of every Great House and beyond, its production sustained by a distributed network of factories from Keystone to Twycross to Pandora.
text.capabilities:
The heart of the BattleMaster lies not in its weaponry but in its cockpit. The lavish command and control systems the Star League designed into the chassis (a roomy cockpit with space for advanced electronics) have saved the design from obsolescence through centuries of technological regression. Even during the darkest years of the Succession Wars, the BattleMaster's generous cockpit provided sufficient gear to make it a preferred ride for unit commanders at every level. All modern variants preserve this key feature, and numerous configurations exploit the available space with command consoles, C3 master computers, or enhanced sensor suites.

In its classic BLR-1G configuration, the BattleMaster carries a Donal PPC in a detachable rifle-style mount for long-range engagement, backed by six Martell medium lasers, four forward-firing surrounding the cockpit and two rear-mounted to discourage flanking attacks. A Holly SRM-6 on the left shoulder and twin SperryBrowning machine guns on the left wrist provide close-range punch and anti-infantry capability. Fourteen and a half tons of StarGuard IV armor give the BattleMaster excellent protection for its weight class, and the VOX 340 fusion engine drives the design at a respectable sixty-four kilometers per hour. The primary weakness of the design is heat management: sustained fire from the full weapons array can overwhelm the eighteen single heat sinks, forcing MechWarriors to exercise fire discipline during prolonged engagements.
text.deployment: A mixed-technology variant also produced by General Motors on El Dorado, this variant is manufactured in limited quantities whenever Clan Sea Fox component supplies are available. A Clan-grade rotary AC/5 occupies the right arm delivering devastating burst fire capability, while an Inner Sphere Streak SRM-6, twin light PPCs, and pair of rear-firing improved heavy medium lasers provide comprehensive coverage at all ranges. Three tons of rotary autocannon ammunition and one ton of Streak reloads are stored in CASE II-protected bays. A light fusion engine provides the necessary power and improves survivability.
text.battleHistory:
The BattleMaster's origins trace to the early twenty-seventh century, when the Star League required a robust, relatively simple assault 'Mech to serve as a comparatively low-technology command platform for non-Royal unit commanders. Hollis Industries answered the call, and by 2633 the first BattleMasters rolled off production lines on Corey. During the great peace of the Star League era, the new design had little opportunity to distinguish itself and was often overlooked in favor of flashier Royal-grade machines. When the Star League crumbled under the ambitions of the Council Lords, however, the sturdy BattleMaster proved its worth while more technologically dependent designs faded into extinction.

The First Succession War devastated Hollis Industries' main factories on Corey, destroying the production lines and scattering finished machines among the competing House forces. Production was sustained through alternative manufacturers, Earthwerks Incorporated on Keystone built for the Free Worlds League, Trellshire Heavy Industries on Twycross served the Lyran Commonwealth, and Red Devil Industries on Pandora eventually joined the production network. Never produced in great numbers, the BattleMaster nonetheless became a common sight across the Inner Sphere as technicians went to extraordinary lengths to keep damaged units operational. Houses Steiner and Marik maintained the largest inventories thanks to their functional production lines, while House Liao fielded a substantial fleet until the Fourth Succession War delivered many into Federated Suns hands.

The Draconis Combine acquired a windfall of advanced BattleMasters through a fortuitous ComStar shipping error, machines intended for Com Guard units arriving instead at Combine depots. These served as excellent command vehicles during the War of 3039. New models incorporating recovered Star League technology were introduced in time for the Clan Invasion, with the Free Worlds League's BLR-3M and the Federated Commonwealth's BLR-3S representing the first major upgrades. The fall of Twycross to Clan Jade Falcon disrupted Trellshire's production, though the world's recapture allowed a brief resumption before the Clan Steel Viper ended BattleMaster manufacturing there to make room for Phoenix Hawk IIC production.

The FedCom Civil War era saw renewed investment in the design. Red Devil Industries on Pandora, long plagued by the planet's corrupt nobility and a haphazard factory layout, finally received refurbishment funds from Archon Katherine Steiner-Davion. A partnership with J.B. BattleMechs Incorporated produced the BLR-4S, though the second Jade Falcon Incursion in 3064 captured Pandora and its new BattleMasters. The Falcons would eventually produce their own Clan-tech variant from the captured factory. Meanwhile, Blankenburg Technologies on Soul began producing Kuritan command variants, and J.B. BattleMechs' own facility on Storfors introduced the revolutionary BLR-10S during the Jihad, emphasizing survivability through a compact engine and heavy-duty gyroscope.

In the post-Jihad era and beyond, the BattleMaster remains in active production across multiple successor states. General Motors on El Dorado builds advanced variants for the Federated Suns, Hollis Industries has resumed limited production on Corey for the Capellan Confederation, and Earthwerks continues output on Keystone. Clan Sea Fox produces its own variant on Twycross, while the Jade Falcon legacy on Pandora persists under changing ownership. Tao MechWorks on Styk has added Capellan production capacity, and the Free Worlds League's Venkateswara facility on Tamarind keeps Marik-spec BattleMasters in service. After nearly five centuries of continuous production and combat deployment, the BattleMaster endures as proof of the virtue of rugged, practical military engineering.
